This paper studies a model of controlled sequential social learning in which an information-mediating planner (e.g., an LLM) controls the information precision of agents while they also learn from the decisions of earlier agents. The modes include investing the maximum allowed resource, not investing any resource, or the investment increasing or decreasing with increase in the belief.
